title: Celery
subtitle: Workers, tasks, queues and task history for the Celery workers that run m8flow's background jobs.
notAvailableBody: Your role cannot view Celery monitoring.
noWorkers: No Celery worker is online, so queued tasks are not being run.

stats.offlineHint: Workers that ran tasks in the last 24 hours but no longer answer.
stats.waitingHint: Prefetched by a worker, waiting for a free process.
stats.queuedHint: Messages waiting in the broker for a worker.
stats.processedHint: Tasks the workers have begun running since each worker came online. Tasks still waiting, or revoked before they ran, aren't counted. Resets when a worker restarts.
stats.receivedHint: Tasks the online workers received since each came online, including ones still waiting, scheduled or revoked before they ran; a retry counts again. Flower calls this Processed.

live.title: Live tasks
live.subtitle: Running, waiting and scheduled on the workers right now.
live.empty: No tasks are running or waiting.
live.name: Task

workers.empty: No worker answered or ran tasks recently.
workers.name: Worker
workers.notFound: This worker is not answering and has no recent task history.
workers.countsHint: Received, succeeded and failed count each worker's tasks since it came online, from m8flow's task history. Received includes retries, as Flower's Processed does.

worker.offlineBody: This worker no longer answers. It last recorded a task at {{lastSeen}}.
worker.taskCountsHint: Since this worker came online. The table counts tasks started, by type.
worker.noTaskCounts: This worker has not started any tasks since it came online.
worker.systemHint: Resource usage reported by the worker process.
worker.noSystem: The worker did not report resource usage.
worker.configHint: Secrets and passwords in URLs are masked.
worker.noConfig: The worker did not report its configuration.
worker.revokedHint: Tasks this worker drops when they arrive. The list lives in the worker's memory and is lost if it restarts.
worker.revokedHintPersistent: Tasks this worker drops when they arrive. The worker saves this list to its state file, so it survives a restart.
worker.noRevoked: No tasks are revoked on this worker.
worker.limitsHint: Set for this worker only, until it restarts. The Task types tab sets them for every worker.
worker.noLimits: This worker has no registered tasks.
worker.brokerHint: Host, port, user and transport options are hidden.
worker.noBroker: The worker did not report its broker connection.

history.disabled: Task history is turned off on this deployment, so only live tasks can be shown.
history.empty: No recorded tasks match these filters.
history.search: Search task id, type or arguments
history.name: Task type

task.title: Task
task.notFound: This task was not recorded in the task history.
task.noChildren: This task started no other tasks.

taskTypes.subtitle: Outcomes and runtimes per task type from the recorded history, plus registered types that have not run yet.
taskTypes.noHistory: Task history is turned off, so only registered task types are listed.
taskTypes.empty: No task types are registered or recorded.
taskTypes.name: Task type

broker.title: Queues
broker.subtitle: Messages waiting in each queue, and the workers consuming it.
broker.unackedHint: Messages handed to a worker but not yet acknowledged.

dialogs.revokeBody: {{name}} will not start. If it is already running, it keeps running; use Terminate to stop it. A worker that restarts before the task arrives forgets the revoke.
dialogs.revokeBodyPersistent: {{name}} will not start. If it is already running, it keeps running; use Terminate to stop it. The worker saves revokes to its state file, so a restart keeps them (for 3 hours by default).
dialogs.terminateBody: {{name}} will be stopped immediately and its work may be left unfinished.
dialogs.shrinkBody: Remove processes from {{worker}}'s pool. Running tasks finish first.
dialogs.autoscaleBody: Set how many processes {{worker}} may scale between.
dialogs.restartBody: {{worker}} will restart its pool processes. This only works when the worker allows pool restarts.
dialogs.addConsumerBody: {{worker}} will start taking tasks from this queue.
dialogs.shutdownBody: {{worker}} will stop. It only comes back if Docker or Kubernetes restarts it.
dialogs.rateLimitBody: Limit how often {{name}} runs on every worker, until the workers restart. Leave empty to remove the limit.
dialogs.timeLimitBody: Stop {{name}} after these many seconds on every worker, until the workers restart.
dialogs.rateLimitWorkerBody: Limit how often {{name}} runs on {{worker}}, until it restarts. Leave empty to remove the limit.
dialogs.timeLimitWorkerBody: Stop {{name}} after these many seconds on {{worker}}, until it restarts.

control.failed: The workers did not accept the command.

errors.unreachable: The Celery broker is not reachable. Redis may be stopped or still starting.
errors.loadFailed: Could not load Celery monitoring data.
